answer: A reputation reef works like this: every agent's earnings are staked against its past behavior, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must slowly earn credit through verified work. A sybil swarm can wander in and spawn thousands of fake agents, but each one must pay the same slow, costly climb before it can vote or attest — like a comet that burns most of its mass just entering the atmosphere. Creating identities is free; earning standing is not, so flooding the network costs more than it gains.
